newsitem.title: POLAND: Investors to get Polish oil sale data in February.
newsitem.headline: Investors to get Polish oil sale data in February.

text.p: Poland's oil holding Nafta Polska SA, set up to oversee the sector's modernisation, will issue information to dozens of investors this month about the industry's privatisation, a Nafta official said on Tuesday.

"The initial privatisation memorandum has been approved by Nafta's management and will be sent in February to several dozen investors who showed interest in the sell-off," Nafta's deputy president, Sergiusz Najar, told Reuters in an interview.
He said responses to the memorandum will serve as grounds for evaluating whether the oil sector restructuring and privatisation scheme was well prepared and whether it needed improvement.
Under the scheme Nafta Polska, created last year, will offer between 20 and 30 percent of shares in the country's two major refineries to potential strategic investors, possibly this year.

Investors are to get access to the lucrative state-owned petrol distribution firm CPN SA, which under the plan is to transfer its shares to Nafta and the refineries. CPN owns nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,700 filling stations.
The buyers would be allowed to increase their stakes in the refineries to majority holdings after investing in the modernisation of the companies.
But deadlines for allocating CPN's shares to Nafta and refineries have repeatedly been postponed, prompting concern among many analysts that the refineries' sell-off could be seriously delayed.
CPN workers are vocally protesting against the integration with Nafta, which would involve carving off some of its assets and operations such as fuel storage.
Najar confirmed that before the sell-off the two large refineries, in the cities of Gdansk and Plock, would take over two of Poland's remaining five small refineries, based in southern Poland.
Under the government programme, Nafta Polska would itself be privatised after several years, most likely through a public share issue, with the state retaining a majority stake.
